questions.q: What is the key difference between a Standard and a Custom fiscal year?
options: Standard fiscal years require Multiple Currencies to be active; custom ones do not
A standard fiscal year is defined by a start month and follows normal calendar periods; a custom fiscal year supports non-calendar periods and cannot be disabled once enabled
A custom fiscal year is only available in Salesforce Classic
There is no functional difference, only a difference in naming
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a standard fiscal year just needs a start month, while a custom fiscal year supports non-calendar period patterns — and once enabled, custom fiscal years are a one-way door.

questions.q: What does activating Multiple Currencies change about the org's corporate currency?
options: It replaces the corporate currency with whichever currency is marked active first
Nothing — the corporate currency stays the same; Multiple Currencies adds the ability to mark additional currencies active alongside it
It removes the concept of a corporate currency entirely
It converts all historical records into the first active currency
questions.explain: The corporate currency is unchanged by activating Multiple Currencies; the feature adds active currencies with their own conversion rates, each rolling up into the same corporate currency.

questions.q: Once a currency is activated in an org with Multiple Currencies enabled, what can be done with it later?
options: It can be deleted entirely if no records use it
It can be deactivated, but it can never be deleted
It can be renamed but not deactivated
Nothing — activation decisions are permanent and unchangeable in every respect
questions.explain: The New Currency form itself warns that a currency cannot be deleted once activated; it can only be deactivated later.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe conversion rate maintenance as "ongoing work, not a one-time setup task"?
options: Because Salesforce automatically deactivates currencies every 90 days
Because conversion rates are manually maintained numbers, and a stale rate means every amount in that currency rolls up incorrectly
Because conversion rates reset to zero every fiscal year
Because only Salesforce Support can update conversion rates
questions.explain: Conversion rates don't update automatically with real exchange rates — an admin has to keep them current, or reporting rollups in that currency become inaccurate.

questions.q: Why does the Fiscal Year setup page recommend exporting data to CSV before changing the fiscal year start month on an existing org?
options: Because changing it shifts every fiscal period going forward and affects opportunities and forecasts organization-wide
Because CSV export is required before any Setup change in Salesforce
Because the fiscal year start month cannot be changed without first deleting all opportunities
Because it has no real effect on data, but Salesforce requires a backup as a formality
questions.explain: The lesson notes this is a serious, data-affecting decision: changing the fiscal year shifts periods and affects forecasts and opportunities org-wide, which is why a backup is recommended first.
